recommendations.title: Close the OpenReply follow-gate loop today — verify, commit, or shelve
recommendations.reason: The uncommitted dm-worker.ts patch is now 48 hours old without a single test run. Each day the patch sits unverified, the probability of a half-remembered state grows while the production risk of an accidental deploy does not decrease. The follow-gate handles lead delivery and DM routing for live campaigns; an untested change sitting on disk is worse than either a tested change in main or a clearly preserved local stash.
recommendations.action: In /root/.hermes/projects/openreply/repo: read AGENTS.md and the lib/queue/dm-worker.ts area, then run `pnpm test -- --reporter=verbose` (or the repo's actual test command from package.json) plus `pnpm typecheck`. Capture the real pass/fail output. If green, commit the two-file change on a topic branch and report the SHA to Chris before any push. If red, fix forward or revert the file with `git checkout -- lib/queue/dm-worker.ts`. Do not run live test comments against any active campaign.

recommendations.title: Resolve the OpenReply branch/worktree state explicitly
recommendations.reason: Main is 3 commits ahead of origin/main and the worktree is dirty. Two consecutive mornings of dreaming-sequence output have flagged this; it is now a discipline problem, not an information problem. Either the patch deserves to ship (in which case it should be on origin) or it deserves to be preserved locally with a written handoff (in which case the working tree should be clean). The current ambiguous state is what bites during the next incident.
